title: WALTEUR Non-Functional Requirements
description: Planguage-quantified non-functional requirements. One entry per NFR. CONSTRAINT: every NFR MUST be measurable — a quality attribute, a unit, a numeric target, and the load_condition the target holds under. A weasel NFR ('the system should be fast', 'highly available') has no unit, no number, and no condition; it is unverifiable and therefore forbidden. Each requirement names the scale (unit), the target (number), and the qualifier (load_condition) — Gilb's Planguage discipline.

unit.description: The scale of measure the target is expressed in (e.g. 'ms', '%', 'rps', 'concurrent_users', 'errors_per_million', 'seconds', 'MB'). Planguage SCALE: an NFR with no unit cannot be measured.

target.description: The numeric target value on the named unit's scale. Planguage GOAL/MUST level. REQUIRED and numeric — a target you cannot put a number on is an aspiration, not a requirement.

load_condition.description: The condition the target must hold under (e.g. 'at 1000 concurrent users', 'p99 under peak Black-Friday load', 'sustained 500 rps for 1h'). Planguage QUALIFIER: a target with no stated condition is meaningless — fast for whom, under what load?

rationale.description: Optional. Why this target was chosen (SLA, benchmark, regulatory floor, competitor parity).

measurement_method.description: Optional. How the target is verified (e.g. 'k6 load test', 'Prometheus histogram p99', 'uptime monitor over 30d'). Planguage METER.
